summary: Defines the sip-trunking-capability link relation type that an enterprise telephony network can use to get a document describing a provider's SIP trunking capabilities and requirements, helping enable peering.

eli5.summary: A company's phone system can find a web page that tells what its phone service provider needs, to connect smoothly.

questions: how to discover sip trunk requirements
what is the sip-trunking-capability link relation
what is a capability set document
subtitle: A link relation that lets an enterprise phone network find a SIP provider's capability document.

tldr.problem: An enterprise SIP network needs to learn the capabilities and configuration requirements of its Internet Telephony Service Provider (ITSP) to set up a SIP trunk.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9409 defines the sip-trunking-capability link relation type, which points to a capability set document, and shows how to discover it with WebFinger.
tldr.outcome: The technical requirements in that document allow seamless peering between SIP-based enterprise telephony networks and the ITSP.

today: RFC 9409 is an Informational document, and no later RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 8288 defines a way to indicate relationships between resources on the Web. This document specifies the sip-trunking-capability link relation type under the rules of RFC 8288.

ITSPs can use it on web resources to provide a structured capability set document. When enterprise telephony devices retrieve it, they can automate the setup of SIP trunking between the two networks.
sections.eli5: It is a label on a web link that says: this link leads to the provider's setup instructions.

sections.title: The Capability Set Document
sections.content:
The ITSP hosts the document through web resources. Its location can be preconfigured and given to each peer, or a central resource can generate the document dynamically from one or more URIs determined by the peering device.

The document describes the configuration parameters needed to establish SIP trunking. It is made of structured, machine-readable parameters that can be converted into configuration data. Its format is documented in the "Automatic Peering for SIP Trunks" draft, not in this RFC.
sections.eli5: It is a checklist the computer can read, listing the settings the provider wants.

sections.title: Example Using WebFinger
sections.content:
In the example, the enterprise device sends a GET to /.well-known/webfinger at the ITSP, asking for the sip-trunking-capability relation. The reply is a JSON Resource Descriptor whose link has an href giving the document's location.

The ITSP may use an authentication framework such as OAuth 2.0 to identify the enterprise network and return the appropriate document.
sections.eli5: The company asks the provider's front desk where the instructions are, and the desk answers with a web address.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
IANA registered the sip-trunking-capability relation in the Link Relation Types registry, referencing RFC 9409.

The relation type is not known to introduce new security issues beyond those in RFC 8288. The RFC recommends caution when publishing potentially sensitive capability information over unencrypted or unauthenticated channels.
sections.eli5: Do not leave private setup notes where just anyone can read them.
